edges.root_basis:
The record of this line starts here. The Braga use is far older -- a 1558
printing is at the Bibliotheque nationale de France and a 1498 printing is
recorded with no digital facsimile located -- and neither is carried in this run,
so no edge is drawn into this station.

That makes this line unusual and worth noticing: it is the ONLY use line in this
file whose root is an act rather than a printing.

THE 1558 PRINTING WAS REACHED AND READ ON 2026-08-02, and this root is kept
anyway. It is BnF Réserve B-1478, 554 canvases, `Missale juxta usum & ordinem
Almae Bracarensis Ecclesiae Hispaniarum Primatis`, dated 1558 by Gallica's own
record, and its shelfmark is pencilled on the flyleaf at canvas f4 beside the
reference `Weale 198` [verified]. Two things in it are worth a later lane's
attention and NEITHER IS ASSERTED AS AN ACT HERE:

  1.  IT CARRIES WHAT LOOKS LIKE ITS OWN PROMULGATING INSTRUMENT. Canvas f5 is a
      letter headed `BALTHASAR LIMPVS ARCHIEPISCOPVS ET BRACARAE Dominus,
      Hispaniarum Primas: Decano & Capitulo sanctae Bracarensis Ecclesiae, ac
      totius eius prouinciae Clero sanctum exoptat spiritum & salutem in Domino
      sempiternam`, in which Archbishop Baltasar Limpo describes finding the old
      missal `corruptum illud certe vetustate` and having a corrected edition
      made [verified in the page image]. That is an archbishop of Braga ordering
      a Braga missal, four hundred years before the act this line is rooted on.
      IT IS NOT ADDED AS A STATION IN THIS RUN: the letter was read but not
      transcribed whole, it carries no date in the portion read, and adding a
      root below an existing root is a change to the line's shape rather than an
      evidence upgrade. It is the single most promising lead for extending this
      line backwards and it is written down so it is not re-found.

  2.  IT WAS PRINTED AT LYON, NOT AT BRAGA. Gallica's record gives the imprint
      as `Lugduni sumptibus Jo. à Burgundia, bibliopolae regis Lusitanorum,
      1558` [verified] -- at Lyon, at the charge of Jean de Bourgogne, bookseller
      to the King of Portugal. Worth recording because this file carries a
      Lyonnais line as well, and a reader meeting `Lugduni` on a Braga book
      should not take it for a use.

  3.  ONE CAUTION ON THE COPY. Its first printed leaf in the digitisation is the
      Limpo letter; no printed title page was found in the leaves examined, and
      the BnF describes the preliminaries as `[10]` leaves. Whether the title
      leaf is absent from this copy was NOT established, and it is flagged
      rather than resolved.
